long_biography.plain_text:
Professional golfer Tiger Woods built TGR Foundation into a lasting education network. He founded it with his parents, Earl and Tida, and moved its emphasis from junior golf clinics towards learning spaces and college access for students from under-resourced communities. The flagship Learning Lab in Anaheim offers practical science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics programmes.

The foundation also links career preparation with mentoring, scholarships and internships through the Earl Woods Scholar Program. Woods’s event business helps fund this work, while additional Learning Labs have carried the model into other American communities. Its programmes now span hands-on enrichment, college readiness and long-term guidance for scholars entering higher education and work.

uncertainties.detail: The immutable display name's middle name ‘Tont’ is unusual but is explicitly confirmed by PGA of America. No correction to the source name is proposed; Tiger is retained as the publicly established nickname.

Woods has income and holdings spanning endorsements, licensing, golf design, events, hospitality, real estate and sports technology. Private valuations and the present percentage contribution of each asset are not publicly stable, so classifications describe the durable mechanism rather than quantify the portfolio.

Woods is simultaneously an athlete, brand licensor, founder and investor. Investor is selected as the best current taxonomy fit because the original fortune arose through performance and endorsement rights and was subsequently deployed across multiple ventures; personal-brand licensing has no separate relationship category.

His father supplied sustained early coaching and both parents supported his development, but reviewed sources do not identify inherited capital, a transferred business or a substantial family-wealth platform. This is treated as ordinary formative family support rather than an inherited or advantaged wealth mechanism.

A current private residence is omitted as unnecessary and potentially transient. No strong evidence establishes a second nationality, so the existing American nationality remains unaltered and the secondary-nationality field remains blank.

The personal website, Instagram, X, Facebook, Forbes and TGR company website are identity-verified. No personal LinkedIn profile cleared the acceptance threshold; the existing Wikipedia record is not duplicated.

The biographies exclude vessel facts, current rankings and net-worth figures, sponsor lists, health and comeback status, private family matters, allegations, controversies, legal issues and other sensitive or transient material.
